sarah_sales: MetroBank POC — they want a multi-region PrivateLink setup where traffic fails over to another region egress with preserved static IPs. Any gotchas? Need rough design + cost delta for the quote.

raj_neteng: Quick q — are they using our Private (VPC) deployment or Hosted? That changes options for PrivateLink + EIP.

sarah_sales: Private deploy (customer VPC) + uses corporate egress appliances in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Wants failover across regions, minimal RTO.

marta_se: Two options usually:
- Active/active: two PrivateLink endpoints + DNS-based failover + region-local NATs (cheaper but harder to preserve source IP)
- Active/passive: primary egress with cross-region NAT failover + floating EIP (via Elastic IP + proxy) — preserves source IPs but adds cost.

raj_neteng: For source IP preservation you need an egress NAT/proxy in each region with static EIP. If traffic must appear from same IP globally you'll need SNAT at the proxy, or use a global Anycast NAT (third-party).

tim_ops: For quick PoC we can suggest an SNI proxy in each region (nginx/haproxy) fronted by an EIP. Health checks and Route53 failover for active/passive.

marta_se: Pricing note: extra EIPs + cross-region data transfer + 2x proxies ~ estimate: $3k-6k/mo per region for low QPS PoC (very rough). I'll add numbers after we know expected QPS.

anna_security: Also flag: PCI/FIN regulatory note — cross-region egress may require data residency controls. Need to confirm with customer. Also request: TLS mTLS to our PrivateLink endpoints? They want audit logs forwarded to their SIEM.

raj_neteng: Minimal firewall rules for PrivateLink and egress proxy:
```
# inbound to proxy EIP (customer control plane)
Allow TCP 443 from customer office IPs / corp ranges
# outbound from proxy to Redwood PrivateLink endpoints
Allow TCP 443 to <redwood-privatelink-endpoint-hostnames>
# health checks from Route53
Allow TCP 443 from Route53 health check IPs
```
And security groups: proxy SG allow 443 from VPC CIDRs, SG for PL endpoint allow 443 from proxy SG.

sarah_sales: Customer asked about AWS PrivateLink vs VPC peering for this use-case — they prefer PrivateLink for isolation. Any quick pros/cons to pass back?

marta_se: PrivateLink = no route table exposure, per-service endpoint, easier firewalling. Peering = lower latency, but requires route propagation and more open routes. For multi-region failover PrivateLink + proxy is simpler operationally.

cloud_broker_bot: Docs: https://redwood.example.com/docs/private-deploy/networking#privatelink-egress-patterns (internal)

sarah_sales: OK I'll consolidate and ask MetroBank for expected QPS + data path residency. @marta_se can you add a 1-pager with config snippets and a cost estimate? :thumbsup: 

marta_se: On it — will drop a short PDF + sample CloudFormation and proxy Helm chart links in this thread later.

tim_ops: For the PoC runbook we should include a smoke test: curl via proxy to confirm source IP + failover by simulating region outage. I can write the steps.

anna_security: Also add KMS envelope keys and that logs stream to their SIEM/S3 with retention policy and audit trail. I'll draft security checklist.

sarah_sales: Perfect. Thanks everyone — looping in account team after we have numbers.
